companyDescription: Defense tech · Switchblade loitering munitions + Puma/JUMP20 drones supplied to Ukraine, now combined with BlueHalo's directed-energy/space/cyber portfolio (post-$4.1B merger) — positioned across air, land, sea, space and cyber for the Golden Dome missile-defense buildout
priceNote: Trading well off the $417.86 52-week high, still digesting the post-BlueHalo integration and a broad defense-sector pullback, but roughly 39% above the $135.20 52-week low set earlier this year — steady contract-award news (Switchblade, P550, ESAero) has kept a floor under the stock ahead of Sept 9 earnings.
summary: AeroVironment's Q1 FY2026 print (late June 2026) was a clean beat — revenue $641.6M vs $559.4M est. (+133% YoY), adjusted EPS $1.84 vs $1.47 est. — and the stock jumped ~19% same-day. Since then, the post-BlueHalo combined entity ($4.1B merger, completed May 2025) has kept landing real, dated contract wins: a $186M Army Switchblade order (Feb 2026), a $200M ESAero acquisition (Mar 2026), and a $117M Army P550 order (2026). Sept 9, 2026 earnings is the next real catalyst to confirm the growth rate is holding as BlueHalo's Golden Dome-relevant directed-energy/space/cyber lines scale alongside the legacy drone business.

catalysts.name: Golden Dome / Contract Award Flow
catalysts.description: Ongoing: $186M Army Switchblade order (Feb 2026), $200M ESAero acquisition (Mar 2026), $117M Army P550 order (2026) — BlueHalo's directed-energy and space/cyber tech is being pitched into the Golden Dome missile-defense initiative, a structural multi-year tailwind rather than a single dated event.

risks: Valuation already reflects real optimism after the post-Q1 rally — the 52-week range ($135.20 to $417.86) shows how sharply this stock can reprice on a single earnings miss vs elevated Street expectations
Two acquisitions in 12 months (BlueHalo $4.1B, ESAero $200M) creates real integration risk — combining air/land/sea/space/cyber product lines and cultures is execution-heavy
Golden Dome and broader defense-budget program timing depends on Congressional appropriations — award schedules can slip regardless of technical readiness
Heavy customer concentration in U.S. government/DoD contracts — a single program cancellation or budget reallocation is a real, demonstrated risk in this sector

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held at 3.50-3.75% on Jul 29, 2026, with 3 of 12 officials dissenting toward a hike — the most hawkish split since 2016. Next FOMC is Sep 15-16, 2026, six days after AVAV's earnings, so no direct overlap this cycle, but a hawkish tilt going into that meeting could still weigh on high-multiple growth names like AVAV into the print.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE still 3.3% YoY, above target — CPI (Aug 12) and jobs data (Aug 7, already printed) are the key data points shaping risk appetite for growth/defense-tech multiples between now and Sept 9 earnings.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Defense spending itself is largely appropriations-driven and not directly rate-sensitive, but AVAV trades at a growth multiple (52-week range of $135-418 shows the multiple compression/expansion swings that come with rate-sensitivity in sentiment, even if the underlying contract backlog is not rate-driven.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — the Golden Dome/BlueHalo contract thesis is largely macro-independent, but AVAV's demonstrated high-beta behavior (proven by its own 52-week range) means a hawkish surprise before Sept 9 could compress the multiple even without touching the underlying fundamentals.
